output.title: Early signs your AI workflow is drifting
output.body:
Eval drift is not a theory problem for a small business; it is a workflow problem. If an AI-assisted process starts giving answers that are inconsistent, off-target, or just a bit too confident for comfort, the question is not whether the model has become sentient. It is whether the workflow still deserves to stay on autopilot.

The practical check is simple: do you already have one repetitive, high-frequency task where AI filters, ranks, or responds to inputs, and would drift show up as customer complaints, missed approvals, failed orders, or manual rework? If the answer is no, there is nothing to monitor yet. If the answer is yes, pick one control and write it down.

A sensible first control is a monthly manual spot-check against a small set of past cases using the original success criteria. Keep the comparison human-readable: what came in, what the system output, and whether a person would still sign off on it. Any threshold you use should be your own operating rule, not a Bareni benchmark.

The next step is to use the free 30-minute diagnostic to ask one clear question: is eval drift a real risk in this workflow, and is the workflow actually live? If it is, Bareni can help define whether drift monitoring belongs in the pilot scope or whether the issue is still too early to tackle. Human approval stays in place before any retraining or policy change. Small business automation works better when it fails politely, not mysteriously.
